f2_target_state.F2-WP-005: IN_PROGRESS / Full telemetry-data spine and collectors

source_observations.finding: UniProf is a cross-runtime profiling orchestrator. It detects a target runtime, delegates to py-spy/0x/rbspy/Excimer/async-profiler/dotnet-trace/perf/Instruments, transforms their differing output formats and applies common hotspot analysis.
source_observations.f2_implication: The strongest transferable mechanism is a normalized measurement adapter contract across profilers, not a new canonical telemetry authority.

source_observations.finding: The PlatformPlugin/ProfileContext interfaces normalize raw artifact types, effective sampling frequency, runtime environment, temporary artifacts, profiler/exporter identity and a ProfileAnalysis summary with total samples/time, profile type, thread/event counts and hotspot self/total/sample/percentile data.
source_observations.f2_implication: F2 can distill a bounded ProfileObservation envelope from these dimensions for WP-005/WP-605/WP-902.

source_observations.finding: ProfileContext/finalizeProfile tracks paths and exporter name but does not bind an immutable F2 causal identity, upstream source commit, profiler binary/image digest, target executable digest, canonical command/effect identity, raw/final artifact digest, privilege mode or explicit uncertainty class.
source_observations.f2_implication: Raw UniProf output is measurement evidence only. An F2 adapter must add exact source/runtime/target/artifact identities and confidence/coverage semantics before admission.

source_observations.finding: Container image selection uses ghcr.io/indragiek/uniprof-<platform>:latest, and platform implementations such as Linux perf likewise default to :latest rather than an immutable digest.
source_observations.f2_implication: An E3/E4 experiment cannot earn exact-source runtime credit from :latest. Any evaluated image must be resolved and pinned by immutable digest/SBOM or rebuilt from exact source.

source_observations.finding: The generic Docker runner adds requested Linux capabilities and escalates to --privileged when SYS_ADMIN is requested. The native Linux perf implementation requests SYS_ADMIN and SYS_PTRACE. The Python container path requests SYS_PTRACE.
source_observations.f2_implication: Default integration must not inherit UniProf privilege choices. Profiling is an explicitly bounded observer operation and must fail closed when required capability exceeds the admitted test surface.

source_observations.finding: Container profiling mounts the host working directory at /workspace without a read-only qualifier. Optional host networking is supported. The profiled target itself is executed inside that environment.
source_observations.f2_implication: UniProf cannot be treated as harmless read-only telemetry by default. The target command still has effect potential; EffectGate/authorized test-harness authority must precede profiling, and workspace/network scope must be constrained independently.

source_observations.finding: The MCP run_profiler tool accepts an exact command string and cwd, translates them into UniProf record arguments and spawns the current runtime to execute the profiler/target workflow. It therefore has command-execution semantics even though its stated purpose is performance measurement.
source_observations.f2_implication: Do not expose UniProf MCP as an autonomous model-side executor. Any future adapter should receive an already-authorized immutable execution receipt/command identity or remain offline over pre-existing profile artifacts.

source_observations.finding: Several platforms default to approximately 999 Hz sampling, including Python and Linux perf. Sampling/event conversion perturbs execution and evented profilers are converted to synthetic weighted samples for common analysis.
source_observations.f2_implication: Cross-profiler numbers are not automatically causally or statistically equivalent. E3 must measure observer overhead and fidelity, and preserve profile_type/sampling_hz/profiler identity rather than flattening them into one unquestioned metric.

source_observations.finding: Meaningful native attribution depends on debug information/frame pointers; perf symbol resolution is documented as best effort and some paths may remain unknown.
source_observations.f2_implication: F2 needs explicit coverage/symbol-resolution quality and UNKNOWN handling. Missing symbols cannot be interpreted as absence of cost.

source_observations.finding: Temporary artifact cleanup is best-effort and finalizeProfile renames the final profile after exporter tagging without creating a cryptographic artifact receipt.
source_observations.f2_implication: F2 must hash and journal the final admitted profile artifact before cleanup/reuse, and preserve raw-artifact lineage when needed for reproducibility.

source_observations.finding: The UniProf repository code is MIT, but its Docker images bundle multiple third-party profilers governed by their own licenses and are explicitly not relicensed by UniProf.
source_observations.f2_implication: Thin contract/distillation is simpler than vendoring the full image stack; any runtime evaluation must record profiler/image component licenses and identities.

source_observations.finding: Upstream says macOS and Linux are supported but development/testing has primarily occurred on macOS; Windows host mode is unsupported. The latest observed repository commit is from 2025-09-13.
source_observations.f2_implication: Linux F2 suitability is an E3 empirical question, not granted by README support claims.

preferred_f2_shape.name: ProfileObservationEnvelope
preferred_f2_shape.authority_rule: The envelope can inform characterization and candidate decisions only. It cannot create canonical world facts, authorize target execution or bypass EffectGate/EffectJournal.

reusable_mechanisms: Runtime/platform plugin interface for profiler selection.
Typed raw-artifact classification before normalized profile conversion.
Common profile analysis contract for hotspot ranking and percentiles.
Offline analyze/visualize separation from record step.

counterhypotheses_and_risks.claim: F2-native telemetry may already provide sufficient CPU/latency/resource characterization, making UniProf-derived profiles redundant.
counterhypotheses_and_risks.discriminator: Compare diagnostic information gain on deterministic hotspot fixtures and real bounded F2 child workloads; retain only signals that materially improve localization beyond native telemetry.

counterhypotheses_and_risks.claim: High-frequency profiling may change scheduler/timing behavior enough to distort the very workload being characterized.
counterhypotheses_and_risks.discriminator: Baseline vs multiple sampling rates with repeated trials; quantify wall/CPU/RSS and hotspot-rank stability.

counterhypotheses_and_risks.claim: Container/privilege/image complexity may outweigh the value of a unified profiler wrapper for F2.
counterhypotheses_and_risks.discriminator: First E3 uses the lowest-privilege Python/py-spy path with immutable image identity; native perf remains blocked unless a separate benefit justifies broader privilege.

counterhypotheses_and_risks.claim: Normalized Speedscope/common analysis may conceal profiler-specific semantics and make cross-runtime comparisons falsely precise.
counterhypotheses_and_risks.discriminator: Preserve profiler/profile_type/sampling_hz and compare normalized results against raw profiler artifacts for known deterministic workloads.

counterhypotheses_and_risks.claim: Source paths/function symbols/profile artifacts can expose sensitive repository structure or content-derived names.
counterhypotheses_and_risks.discriminator: Run a profile artifact secret/path-sensitivity fence before persistence or cross-repo research ingestion; redact presentation without mutating canonical evidence digests.

next_exact_discriminator.goal: Determine whether UniProf's lowest-privilege practical path adds reproducible diagnostic value beyond F2 native telemetry at acceptable observer cost.
preconditions: Use an explicitly authorized zero-cost isolated Linux test surface.
No real external effect, no paid provider, no external network dependency.
Resolve exact UniProf source/package and py-spy/container image digest before run; do not use mutable :latest as evidence identity.
Do not grant SYS_ADMIN or --privileged. Start with Python/py-spy and only SYS_PTRACE if the admitted sandbox allows it.
Use a disposable/read-only source fixture plus explicitly writable temporary output area rather than a valuable workspace mount.
next_exact_discriminator.fixture: Deterministic local Python program with two known CPU hotspots of intentionally different cost plus one child process, fixed inputs and no network/filesystem effects outside the temporary test directory.
comparison: UniProf Python profile at a lower sampling rate
UniProf Python profile at upstream default 999 Hz
measure: hotspot rank and share accuracy against known fixture structure
failure behavior when SYS_PTRACE is unavailable
next_exact_discriminator.promotion_rule: E3 only if the exact-source/digest-bound run reproduces useful profiling with scoped privileges and explicit overhead. E4 requires comparison against exact F2 native telemetry. E5 requires reproducible net benefit and a minimal F2-owned adapter design. E6 remains Trigger4-only.
